reading.body:
Organizations can run AI models entirely on their own hardware using six major open-source tools, avoiding vendor lock-in and external data transmission.

Self-hosted inference has become viable at scale. Ollama and llama.cpp allow local model execution with minimal infrastructure. vLLM handles high-throughput workloads on self-owned hardware. PyTorch and TensorFlow provide the frameworks for training and deployment pipelines. Hugging Face operates as the central model registry, though it introduces a supply-chain dependency. The common thread across all six is elimination of data upload to external inference APIs.

For AI scaling specifically, this matters because compute that runs locally does not require network bandwidth to cloud providers, and models can be deployed to edge hardware, data centers, or on-premises clusters without vendor approval. This shifts the constraint from cloud capacity to building space, power provisioning, and cooling at the deployment site. Organizations can now bind their AI spending directly to their own infrastructure investments rather than cloud pricing.

What this collection does not cover: production governance, model verification, or how to validate that downloaded models have not been poisoned or modified. The data flags "model provenance tracking" and "supply-chain verification needed" as known gaps, not solved problems. Likewise, cost of deployment, throughput benchmarks, and scaling limits for each tool are absent. The page establishes that self-hosting is possible, not that it is optimal for any specific workload.
